title: Managing bioelectric connectivity induces or suppresses cancer independent of genetics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Managing bioelectric connectivity induces or suppresses cancer independent of genetics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Managing bioelectric connectivity between cells can override genetically determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a wild-type background or suppressing tumorigenesis driven by strong oncogenes such as p53 or KRAS mutations, so genetic alterations are not necessary either to induce or to revert cancer.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed, recent data show that managing this connectivity can override default genetically-determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a perfectly wild-type background (Blackiston et al., 2011) or suppressing tumorigenesis induced by strong oncogenes like p53 or KRAS mutations (Chernet and Levin, 2013a,b).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos (melanocyte conversion and oncogene-induced tumour-like structures)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-24: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The induction and suppression endpoints are experimentally concrete and published. Existing data can assess the specific Xenopus demonstrations, but the broad independence-from-genetics conclusion exceeds their scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare melanoma-like conversion and oncogene-induced tumor incidence across bioelectric or connectivity manipulations and matched controls, verifying genotype and measuring whether intervention changes tumor phenotypes independently of mutation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw embryo-level outcomes may not be deposited.

Connectivity and membrane voltage interventions may have off-target effects.

The Xenopus tumor-like phenotypes do not cover cancer generally.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.4
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Incidence of the reported Xenopus phenotypes under voltage manipulation, with and without oncogenes, is published with controls and covers the claim's stated embryo scope. Those numbers can be audited and cannot be recomputed from raw images, because no image or count archive was released. The jump from these foci to metastatic melanoma in general is outside what the measurements contain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score melanocyte conversion in wild-type Xenopus after a bioelectric perturbation, and score tumor-like structures in p53 or KRAS backgrounds with and without a normalizing voltage manipulation; override holds if incidence moves in the predicted direction on a wild-type genome.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Counts are in the Xenopus papers, not a deposited animal-level table.

The positive series are from one laboratory.

The readouts are embryo pigment and tumor-like foci, a narrow stand-in for metastatic melanoma and clinical reversion.

operationalizability: 0.75

analysis feasibility: 0.4
